table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER I
table_of_contents.title: Treats of the Place where Oliver Twist was Bom ; and of the Circumstances attending his Birth

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER II
table_of_contents.title: Treats of Oliver Twist's Growth, Education, and Board

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER III
table_of_contents.title: Relates how Oliver Twist was very near getting a Place, which would not have been a Sinecure

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER IV
table_of_contents.title: Oliver, being offered another Place, makes his first Entry into Public Life

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER V
table_of_contents.title: Oliver mingles with new Associates. Going to a Funeral for the first Time, he forms an unfavourable Notion of his Master's Business

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER VI
table_of_contents.title: Oliver, being goaded by the Taunts of Noah, rouses into Action, and rather astonishes him

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER VII
table_of_contents.title: Oliver continues refractory

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER VIII
table_of_contents.title: Oliver walks to London. He encounters on the Road a Strange sort of young Gentleman

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER IX
table_of_contents.title: Containing further Particulars concerning the pleasant old Gentleman, and his hopeful Pupils

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER X
table_of_contents.title: Oliver becomes better acquainted with the Characters of his new Associates ; and purchases Experience at a high Price. Being a short, but very important Chapter, in this History

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XI
table_of_contents.title: Treats of Mr. Fang the Police Magistrate ; and furnishes a slight Specimen of his Mode of administering Justice

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XII
table_of_contents.title: In which Oliver is taken better Care of, than he ever was before. And in which the Narrative reverts to the merry old Gentleman and his youthful Friends

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XIII
table_of_contents.title: Some new Acquaintances are introduced to the intelligent Reader ; connected with whom various pleasant Matters are related, appertaining to this History

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XIV
table_of_contents.title: Comprising further Particulars of Oliver's Stay at Mr. Brownlow's. With the remarkable Prediction which one Mr. Grimwig uttered concerning him, when he went out on an Errand

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XV
table_of_contents.title: Showing how very fond of Oliver Twist, the merry old Jew and Miss Nancy were

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XVI
table_of_contents.title: Relates what became of Oliver Twist after he had been claimed by Nancy

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XVII
table_of_contents.title: Oliver's Destiny continuing unpropitious, brings a Great Man to London to injure his Reputation

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XVIII
table_of_contents.title: How Oliver passed his Time, in the improving Society of his reputable Friends

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XIX
table_of_contents.title: In which a notable Plan is discussed and determined on

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XX
table_of_contents.title: Wherein Oliver is delivered over to Mr. William Sikes

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXI
table_of_contents.title: The Expedition

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXII
table_of_contents.title: The Burglary

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXIII
table_of_contents.title: Which contains the Substance of a pleasant Conversation between Mr. Bumble and a Lady ; and shows that even a Beadle may be susceptible on some Points

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXIV
table_of_contents.title: Treats of a very poor Subject, But is a short one ; and may be found of Importance in this History

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXV
table_of_contents.title: Wherein this History reverts to Mr. Fagin and Company

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXVI
table_of_contents.title: In which a mysterious Character appears upon the Scene ; and many Things, inseparable from this History, are done and performed

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXVII
table_of_contents.title: Atones for the Unpoliteness of a former Chapter ; which deserted a Lady, most unceremoniously

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXVIII
table_of_contents.title: Looks after Oliver, and proceeds with his Adventures

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXIX
table_of_contents.title: Has an introductory Account of the Inmates of the House to which Oliver resorted

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXX
table_of_contents.title: Relates what Oliver's new Visitors thought of him

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXI
table_of_contents.title: Involves a critical Position

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXII
table_of_contents.title: Of the happy Life Oliver began to lead with his kind Friends

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXIII
table_of_contents.title: Wherein the Happiness of Oliver and his Friends experiences a sudden Check

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXIV
table_of_contents.title: Contains some introductory Particulars relative to a young Gentleman who now arrives upon the Scene ; and a new Adventure which happened to Oliver

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXV
table_of_contents.title: Containing the unsatisfactory Result of Oliver's Adventure ; and a Conversation of some Importance between Harry Maylie and Rose

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXVI
table_of_contents.title: Is a very short one, and may appear of no great Importance in its Place. But it should be read notwithstanding, as a Sequel to the last, and a Key to one that will follow when its Time arrives

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXVII
table_of_contents.title: In which the Reader may perceive a Contrast, not uncommon in matrimonial Cases

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXVIII
table_of_contents.title: Containing an Account of what passed between Mr. and Mrs. Bumble, and Mr. Monks, at their nocturnal Interview

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XXXIX
table_of_contents.title: Introduces some respectable Characters with whom the Reader is already acquainted, and shows how Monks and the Jew laid their worthy Heads together

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XL
table_of_contents.title: A strange Interview, which is a Sequel to the last Chapter

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLI
table_of_contents.title: Containing fresh Discoveries, and showing that Surprises, like Misfortunes, seldom come alone

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLII
table_of_contents.title: An old Acquaintance of Oliver's, exhibiting decided Marks of Genius, becomes a public Character in the Metropolis

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLIII
table_of_contents.title: Wherein is shown how the Artful Dodger got into Trouble

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLIV
table_of_contents.title: The Time arrives for Nancy to redeem her Pledge to Rose Maylie. She fails

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLV
table_of_contents.title: Noah Claypole is employed by Fagin on a secret Mission

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLVI
table_of_contents.title: The Appointment kept

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLVII
table_of_contents.title: Fatal Consequences

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLVIII
table_of_contents.title: The Flight of Sikes

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER XLIX
table_of_contents.title: Monks and Mr. Brownlow at length meet. Their Conversation, and the Intelligence that interrupts it

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER L
table_of_contents.title: The Pursuit and Escape

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER LI
table_of_contents.title: Affording an Explanation of more Mysteries than one, and comprehending a Proposal of Marriage with no Word of Settlement or Pin-money

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER LII
table_of_contents.title: The Jew's Last Night alive

table_of_contents.label: CHAPTER LIII
table_of_contents.title: And Last

title: The Adventures of Oliver Twist
by_statement: With introd. and notes by Andrew Lang.  In one vol. with the original illus
